title: Best Storyboard Artists (2026): Plan Videos, Ads and Films
description: How to hire a storyboard artist for ads, animation, films or explainers: frame counts, style, how to brief it, what drives the price and red flags.
intro: Storyboard artists turn a script into a sequence of drawings that show each shot: framing, action and camera movement. Storyboards help teams agree on a video before money is spent on filming or animation. Projects go wrong when the script is not final, the style is more detailed than needed, or frames do not show the information the production team needs. This guide helps you get storyboards that make production easier.

faq.q: How many frames do I need?
faq.a: It depends on the script and number of shots. A short ad may need a few frames, a longer explainer many more. The artist can estimate from your script.
Rough boards are faster and fine for internal planning. Detailed or colored boards help when pitching to clients or investors.

faq.q: Do I need a final script first?
faq.a: Yes, or very close. Script changes after drawing often mean redrawing frames.
Usually the shot type, action, camera movement and notes on dialogue or sound.

faq.q: Can the storyboard become an animatic?
faq.a: Many artists can time the frames to a voice-over or music as a simple animatic. Ask if you need it.
